transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been really struggling to finish tasks and follow through on instructions, whether at work or at home. On top of that, I feel constantly restless and find myself fidgeting all the time. It's making it really hard to get things done, so I wanted to see if I could get some help.
Can you tell me more about your difficulty finishing tasks - is it because you have trouble paying attention to details, get distracted easily, or something else?

To be honest, I'm not entirely sure of the exact reason, like whether it's distraction or missing details. I just know that I struggle significantly with following through on instructions and finishing chores or work projects. I frequently find myself failing to complete things that I start.
Do you often act impulsively, interrupt others, or have trouble waiting for your turn, in addition to the restlessness and fidgeting you mentioned?

No, I don't really experience those specific issues like acting impulsively, interrupting others, or having trouble waiting my turn. The restlessness and fidgeting I mentioned earlier are definitely the main physical symptoms I deal with on a daily basis.
Can you estimate how often you lose things, forget appointments or tasks, or have difficulty organizing your time and tasks, and how much this affects your daily life?

I lose important things like my keys, wallet, and work materials almost daily, and this has been a constant struggle for nearly two years now—about a year and eleven months. It makes me feel completely disorganized and causes a lot of stress because I just can't seem to keep track of my belongings or follow through on my daily duties.
Do you think your restlessness and fidgeting are separate issues from your difficulties with organization and task completion, or do they seem to be connected in some way?

I definitely feel like they are connected. When I'm feeling really restless and constantly fidgeting, it makes it almost impossible to sit still and focus on my work. That physical restlessness just makes it so much harder to follow through on my tasks or keep track of where I'm putting my things.
Can you tell me at what age you first started experiencing these symptoms of restlessness, fidgeting, and difficulty with task completion, and have they been consistent over time?

I actually first started experiencing these kinds of issues when I was a kid, definitely before I turned 12 years old. However, they have been consistently present and causing real problems for about 1 year and 11 months now.

Looking back, did you experience significant symptoms of inattention, such as disorganization, forgetfulness, or difficulty sustaining focus, during your childhood, even if the restlessness and fidgeting were also present?

Yes, looking back, those issues definitely started in my childhood before I was 12. Even as a kid, I had a really hard time finishing my schoolwork or chores and was constantly losing my things. On top of that, I was always fidgeting in my seat and feeling incredibly restless.
During your childhood, were you more likely to be described as a restless, fidgety, and 'always on the go' type of child, or was it more about being disorganized and having trouble paying attention?

Honestly, I was described as both. I was incredibly restless and fidgety, always tapping my feet, squirming, and unable to sit still. At the same time, I struggled a lot with disorganization and attention, constantly losing my things and failing to finish my chores or schoolwork.

So, just to confirm, you have experienced significant symptoms of both inattention, such as disorganization and difficulty sustaining focus, and hyperactivity, such as restlessness and fidgeting, throughout your life, including childhood, and these symptoms have been causing significant impairment in your daily life?

Yes, that's absolutely correct. The fidgeting, restlessness, difficulty finishing tasks, and constantly losing my things started way back in childhood before I was 12. They have caused significant impairment in my daily life, especially over the last year and 11 months.
It sounds like you've experienced a combination of symptoms throughout your life, including both inattention and hyperactivity. Is that a fair summary of what you've shared with me today?

Yes, that is a highly accurate summary of what I've been dealing with. I definitely struggle with both sides of this—having trouble focusing and losing things, as well as feeling constantly restless and fidgety. All of these challenges have indeed been present since my childhood, well before I turned 12.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of both inattention (disorganization, difficulty sustaining focus, losing things) and hyperactivity (restlessness, fidgeting) have been present since childhood, and they have caused significant impairment in daily life. The patient's description of their symptoms and their onset in childhood, before the age of 12, aligns with the diagnostic criteria for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation). The previous candidate of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation) is less likely because the patient also experiences significant hyperactivity symptoms. The patient's lack of impulsivity symptoms, such as acting impulsively or interrupting others, does not rule out the Combined Presentation diagnosis, as this subtype requires symptoms of both inattention and hyperactivity, but not necessarily impulsivity. Therefore, the current candidate is Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation).
